title: Conformant planning, growing horizon
description: The conformant planning loop without a bound constant: the horizon grows by one step at a time (A.ground, G.extend, C.ground), an external query(t) asks for the goal at the current horizon, and the first horizon with a plan gives the shortest plans.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The room, the moves and the horizon. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
free(X,Y) :- cell(X,Y), not pillar(X,Y).
% The four moves.
dir(e,1,0). dir(w,-1,0). dir(n,0,1). dir(s,0,-1).
% to(X,Y,D,X2,Y2): moving in direction D from (X,Y) leads to (X2,Y2). A move against
% a wall or the pillar leaves the robot where it is.
to(X,Y,D,X+DX,Y+DY) :- free(X,Y), dir(D,DX,DY), free(X+DX,Y+DY).
to(X,Y,D,X,Y)       :- free(X,Y), dir(D,DX,DY), not free(X+DX,Y+DY).

#program step(t).
% Step t exists once the horizon reaches it.
step(t).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): any sequence of t moves.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: one move per step, for the steps grounded so far.
#show do/2.
#program step(t).
1 { do(t,D) : dir(D,_,_) } 1.
% query(t): the plan has to reach the goal at step t (true for the current horizon only).
#external query(t).

fragments.name: refine
fragments.description: Grounded once per counterexample: the plan must also work from that start cell.
fragments.text:
#program refine(k).
% cex(k,start(X,Y)): the k-th counterexample is a start cell. Follow the plan from there ...
at(k,X,Y,0) :- cex(k,start(X,Y)).
at(k,X2,Y2,T) :- at(k,X,Y,T-1), do(T,D), to(X,Y,D,X2,Y2).
% ... it has to end in the goal at the horizon being queried.
:- goal(X,Y), query(T), not at(k,X,Y,T).

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the moves of the plan.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a start cell from which the plan does not reach the goal (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: a start cell from which the plan ends somewhere else at the horizon.
1 { start(X,Y) : free(X,Y) } 1.
at(X,Y,0) :- start(X,Y).
#program step(t).
at(X2,Y2,t) :- at(X,Y,t-1), do(t,D), to(X,Y,D,X2,Y2).
#external query(t).
:- goal(X,Y), at(X,Y,T), query(T).
#show start/2.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction + refine
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# No bound constant: the horizon t grows until a plan exists. Each round grounds step t in
# A, makes the new do(t,D) atoms interface atoms (G.extend, before C grounds the step that
# reads them), grounds step t in C, and moves the external query from t - 1 to t.
# Refinements of shorter horizons stay: a start cell refutes a plan prefix only through
# query(T), so they are inactive at the new horizon (sound, only weaker).
t = 0
found = false
while not found:
    t = t + 1
    A.ground(step, t)
    G.extend(step, t)
    C.ground(step, t)
    if t > 1:
        A.set(A.atom("query", t - 1), false)
        C.set(C.atom("query", t - 1), false)
    A.set(A.atom("query", t), true)
    C.set(C.atom("query", t), true)
    loop:
        M = A.solve()
        if not M: break
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            A.expand(refine, cex = X.atoms(start/2))
        else:
            accept M
            A.add(G.block(M))
            found = true
log "shortest horizon:", t

instances.facts:
% A robot in a 4 x 4 room with one pillar. It does not know where it starts.
cell(1..4,1..4).
pillar(2,3).
goal(2,2).

% A 3 x 3 room without a pillar; the goal is a corner.
cell(1..3,1..3).
#defined pillar/2.
goal(1,1).
% The shortest plans have 4 moves.

% A corridor of 5 x 1 cells; the goal is in the middle. Moves n and s do nothing.
cell(1..5,1).
#defined pillar/2.
goal(3,1).
% The shortest plans have 6 moves.
